titre: Paula Reichenberg featured by UBS for her approach to leadership
texte:
We are proud to announce that our CEO and founder, Paula Reichenberg, has been featured by UBS in a LinkedIn post on her distinctive approach to leadership: building on transparency, expertise and the strength of a well-chosen team.

For Paula, self-reflection and openness are not weaknesses. They are major strengths, especially in fast-growing start-ups, where strong collaboration is essential to success.

At Neur.on AI Solutions, Paula applies this philosophy to lead our LegalTech innovation. Her aim: secure, AI-based solutions that simplify the complex multilingual workflows of lawyers and international legal experts.

View the LinkedIn post.

titre: Paula Reichenberg at LegalTechTalk in London, 26 and 27 June 2025
texte:
Neur.on CEO Paula Reichenberg will attend LegalTechTalk on 26 and 27 June at the InterContinental London - The O2. With more than 4,000 participants and over 300 speakers, LegalTechTalk has become one of the most influential legal innovation events in Europe.

After speaking at the 2024 edition, Paula returns this year to meet legal professionals, heads of legal departments and technologists who are driving AI adoption in the legal sector. The 2025 focus on AI, data and workflow integration fits Neur.on’s mission closely: to transform legal translation with advanced technology built into everyday work tools.

During the event, Paula will also record a special podcast episode with Robert Hanna, host of the Legally Speaking Podcast. It will further raise Neur.on’s profile where law and technology meet.

titre: Neur.on at the 12th Anwaltskongress of the Swiss Bar Association in Lucerne
texte:
Our CEO, Paula Reichenberg, joined legal professionals from across Switzerland at the 12th Anwaltskongress in Lucerne, the flagship event of the Swiss Bar Association.

This year’s congress focused on the digital transformation of law, with sessions on Justitia 4.0, AI tools and the changing LegalTech landscape. Paula took the opportunity to meet law firms, technology providers and institutional leaders. She presented Neur.on’s AI legal translation platform as a key solution for a legal ecosystem that is going digital fast.

The strong interest in multilingual workflows and in the efficiency gains that technology brings confirms a growing demand across the Swiss legal sector. It supports Neur.on’s mission and its momentum in the market.

titre: Paula Reichenberg presents Neur.on at the TLTF Summit 2024
texte:
At the TLTF Summit 2024, Neur.on CEO Paula Reichenberg took the stage to present our AI solution for automating legal translation workflows.

Our tool is built directly into Microsoft Word. It uses the latest advances in language models to help legal professionals work faster and more accurately, without changing their habits. In her pitch, Paula also shared our vision for the future of agentic AI in legal operations, where smart tools fit naturally into everyday legal workflows.

Watch the full pitch on YouTube.

titre: Neur.on featured by TLTF among the 2024 Startup Showcase start-ups
texte:
We are proud to share that TLTF recently featured Neur.on in its follow-up on the start-ups that stood out at the Startup Showcase of the TLTF Summit 2024.

Our CEO and founder, Paula Reichenberg, presented our AI suite there, designed to automate legal translation workflows. Our technology is fully integrated into Microsoft Word. It combines the latest generation of language models with a smart co-pilot, so that legal teams can deliver faster and more accurate translations with minimal friction.

Looking ahead, we believe that agentic AI translation will redefine self-service in legal settings. It will make self-service not only feasible but truly intuitive and empowering for legal professionals.

As we grow, our mission remains clear: to offer clean interfaces, designed for lawyers and built into the tools that firms already use, such as MS Word, Contract Express and Relativity.

View the LinkedIn post.

titre: Neur.on’s CEO at Legalweek in New York, 26 and 27 March 2025
texte:
One ear firmly on the ground, the other keenly up in the air… This is how our CEO, Paula Reichenberg, watches the market and anticipates trends to guide Neur.on’s business development.

“To do that, you sometimes have to go where the strongest signals come from,” she said.

“That is exactly why, this afternoon, I found myself at the airport, waiting for a flight to New York.”

This week, Paula is attending Legalweek in New York, a flagship event that has always been at the forefront of major technological change in the legal sector.

texte:

“At the time, you heard about the sneaker brand ‘On’ everywhere. We just said: ‘Well, we’re Neur-On now.’”

“I’m superstitious about these things, and I don’t want to jinx myself.”

titre: Paula Reichenberg shares her mistakes on stage at the Digital Economy Award 2024
texte:
Learn from Neur.on’s CEO as she shares her mistakes on stage to help you avoid them.

When you scroll through LinkedIn, 97% of posts talk about success. The upsides, the travel, the smiling networking photos. (We know, of course, that we all do it, even Paula.)

Of the remaining 3%, two per cent argue for more honest communication about failures and mistakes.

And the last one per cent REALLY shows the missteps, so that others can learn from them and avoid them.

Paula Reichenberg, CEO of Neur.on, is a strong advocate of learning from mistakes. If you would like to learn from hers, save the date: 14 November.

Paula will speak at the Digital Economy Award 2024 at the Hallenstadion in Zurich, at the ‘AI Sandbox’ event to be precise.

From 3pm to 4pm, Andrea Fossati of Parquery, Cristiano Malossi of IBM Research and Paula will discuss what they experienced in their past ventures.

titre: Information security: Neur.on achieves ISO 27001 certification
texte:
What do you think is the main concern of LegalTech and FinTech companies when they work with new suppliers? In our experience, it is information security.

After all, in these sectors, handling client data according to protocol is not a gimmicky extra. It is absolutely essential.

And while our smiling faces may not show it, we take this subject very seriously. So seriously that we have achieved ISO 27001 certification.

ISO 27001 is an international standard for implementing, maintaining and improving ISMS (information security management systems).

Our processes for accessing, storing and protecting information have been thoroughly checked by an official third-party body.

And as you can imagine, we will not stop there: this T-shirt is only the first in our security fashionista’s wardrobe. More will be printed soon. Because IT security is already woven into everything we do.

titre: BILANZ 2024 ranking: Neur.on 13th among the most innovative companies and 2nd for innovation culture
texte:

Neur.on appears twice: in the overall ranking of the top 80 most innovative Swiss companies, we reached 13th place. And in the ‘Innovation Culture’ category, we even came second. (Congratulations to Numarics on taking pole position.)

It really pays not only to nurture a fast-paced team of thinkers, testers and tinkerers, but also to let that team fully live this culture of open innovation. So much so that it is ready to share its satisfaction if major national publications or a well-known statistics portal were, hypothetically, to send your team survey links about how you work internally. (Just in case, you know.)

Read the two-page feature now in the MARKETS, Innovation section of the e-paper.

titre: Neur.on joins the Kickstart Innovation cohort in the Finance & Insurance vertical
texte:

At the opening ceremony on Tuesday, the entrepreneurial spirit was palpable, and I had the pleasure of pitching Neur.on to the programme partners, investors and my peers.

Now follows a week of talks and meetings in Zurich and Fribourg with national and international collaboration partners, experienced mentors, subject-matter specialists and like-minded colleagues.

What is the goal of all this? Kickstart Innovation helps us find new clients by matching them with our respective cohorts and starting the conversation. All under the watchful eye of the Kickstart team, and in particular of Katka Letzing, whose favourite line is: “If you don’t sign PoC agreements by the end of the month, I will find you.”

The highly motivated people around me are Pascal Sollberger and Tobias Wegmüller (both at hypt), Markus Geissler and Elisabetta Maria Chiarantoni (both at Kickstart Innovation), Ravina Mutha of enterprisebot, and Mathias Höllerl of Keyless.

titre: LegalTechTalk 2024 in London: three gold nuggets on reinventing law firms
texte:
How law firms are reinventing their operating models and their relationships with general counsel: three gold nuggets from Legal Innovation panellists at LegalTechTalk 2024 in London.

  • Invest in the relationship between in-house legal teams or general counsel and external counsel, and develop it. It is the easiest way to obtain practical and proactive legal advice.
  • Analyse your processes and data to achieve marginal efficiency gains. To innovate in a law firm, start with low-risk areas, then gradually move on to more complex processes.
  • Build multidisciplinary teams that bring together the key departments concerned, to meet the client’s requirements and offer a holistic client experience.

These insights come from James Lane, Jordan Lee and Line Lolk Thomsen, with whom Neur.on CEO Paula Reichenberg discussed the topic “How Law Firms Reinvent their Operating Models and Relationships with General Counsels”.

titre: Neur.on wins the Swiss FinTech Awards 2024 in the Early-Stage category
texte:
It felt like coming home…

Last night, the jury of the Swiss FinTech Awards 2024 named Neur.on the winner of the ‘Early-Stage Startup’ category.

Having pitched in many places, we usually come across the same questions. “Why would I need a specialised AI-powered translation engine?” “Haven’t you heard of DeepL?” “My six-year-old could translate this document online.”

But the Swiss FinTech Awards were different.

Here, it felt as if the whole room GOT us. The people there knew that an ordinary online translation service can guarantee neither a secure platform for client data nor language that is specific to the finance and legal markets and matches the professionalism expected of them.

Thank you, Swiss FinTech Awards, for that warm feeling of finally being at home.

texte:

From the relevance of machine translation to practical case studies and recommendations for the future use and development of translation technologies, the study covers every aspect.

Read the full study, in German and English.

titre: SAV Female Lawyers’ Day in Bern, 5 February 2024: inspiring career paths
texte:
From the group general counsel of a global company to partners at international law firms, the Female Lawyers’ Day (Journée des Avocates, Tag der Anwältinnen), organised in Bern by the Swiss Bar Association (Schweizerischer Anwaltsverband, SAV) on 5 February 2024, brought together inspiring women from all walks of life.

Are women lawyers more prone to ‘professional accidents’?

Surprisingly, one theme kept coming up in their remarkable careers: they attributed their success to ‘accidents’ (‘un concours de circonstances’ or ‘Zufall’).

Yet as we listened to their stories, it became clear that excellence, boldness, strategic seizing of opportunities and authenticity are far more plausible explanations.

Many thanks to the wonderful organiser, Sandra De Vito Bieri, for setting up this mentoring opportunity. Thanks also to Birgit Sambeth for bringing the Female Lawyers’ Day to life. To all the moderators and panellists: thank you for your candid stories and valuable advice.

titre: AI for translation in public administration: Neur.on at the Innovation Sandbox
texte:
AI-based tools can be used in many areas. But what potential does AI offer for translation in public administrations?

Neur.on thanks Zurich for fostering an environment where LegalTech start-ups can thrive. It allows us to show how we can make public administration more efficient. We want to transform services through innovation, for a more effective, citizen-centred approach.

In this Innovation Sandbox, Paula Reichenberg, CEO and founder of Neur.on, and Simona Todesco, COO of Textshuttle, together with Raphael von Thiessen, explain the challenges of legal translation with specialised artificial intelligence and show how to produce secure and adaptable machine translations.

Watch now: https://youtu.be/yZKDzhTlfcA

The Innovation Sandbox for Artificial Intelligence is an initiative in which public administration, business and research work together on regulatory issues and enable the use of new types of data sources. It is a test environment for implementing AI projects, designed to promote responsible innovation.

titre: Paula Reichenberg, SLTA Vice-President, at the OAF Training Day 2023
texte:
As Vice-President of the Swiss LegalTech Association (SLTA), Neur.on CEO Paula Reichenberg took part in the OAF Training Day 2023, hosted by the Fribourg Bar on Friday 1 December 2023.

The event, organised by the Ordre des Avocats Fribourgeois (OAF), gave legal professionals a practical overview of several key topics, including the implications of the new Data Protection Act for law firms and best practices in data management.

The workshop answered specific questions: how long law firms must keep their clients’ files, whether it is lawful to use client data to train an AI, and how to implement cookie banners on websites.

Through this event, the SLTA Fribourg chapter reaffirmed its commitment to providing clear and precise answers to complex and uncertain legal questions.

About the speakers:

Michael Montavon, Doctor of Law, legal adviser at the Legislation Department of the Canton of Fribourg, lecturer in e-government, data protection and legislative drafting.

Paula Reichenberg, lic. iur. Fribourg, lawyer registered with the Zurich Bar, CEO and founder of Neur.on AI Solutions, Vice-President of the Swiss LegalTech Association and Digital Shaper 2023.

titre: Weblaw.ch BrownBag on 29 November 2023: legal translation with specialised AI
texte:
On 29 November at 1pm (CET), join us for a special BrownBag on Zoom organised by Weblaw.ch, with a presentation by our CEO on “Do-it-Yourself Legal Translation with the Help of Specialized AI: Insider Tips & Best Practices”.

This informative session will shed light on the transformative potential of AI in legal translation and offer valuable tips for streamlining your legal translation projects.

We all know how to use DeepL to translate half a page quickly.

But what about a 60-page contract, or 500 pages of exhibits in highly confidential arbitration proceedings? What can AI do to help you, and what are the best practices for running a legal translation project efficiently?

Solving the challenges of legal translation with specialised AI: that is Neur.on’s mission.

At this BrownBag lunch, you will learn about the new possibilities offered by the latest technology, along with tools you can use right away to work more efficiently and turn tedious legal translations into a real pleasure.

Go to the meeting link.

titre: Le Temps names Paula Reichenberg to its 2023 ‘Forum des 100’
texte:
Le Temps has named Neur.on’s CEO a member of the ‘Forum des 100’, which recognises 100 influential figures who have done much to raise the profile of French-speaking Switzerland in 2023.

By naming our CEO, Paula Reichenberg, among the 100 figures who raise the profile of French-speaking Switzerland, Le Temps highlights the importance of efficient, high-quality legal translation solutions for our country’s competitiveness and digital fitness.

In an increasingly multipolar world, a precise and reliable understanding of foreign legal concepts and documents is key to economic and political success.

Swiss data sovereignty and security are essential for impartial negotiations and for a proactive defence against power struggles between intelligence services.

Today, at the SwissTech Convention Center of EPFL (Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne), Dominique Mégret of Swisscom Ventures highlighted Switzerland’s ‘luxury watchmaking’ DNA, present in every sector. Wherever great precision, the ability to decode complexity and an understanding of global diversity are required, we have a natural advantage. Let us build on this strength by investing the human and financial resources needed for Swiss digital innovation to succeed globally.

titre: Paula Reichenberg at the AIBL lunch in Geneva on legal tech and generative AI
texte:

So far, legal tech has not lived up to its promise. The expected revolution never happened. Will the new wave of technology around generative AI and other tools finally change the way lawyers work?

To register for this event, write to info@aibl.ch.

titre: Paula Reichenberg joins the Industrial Board of the Swiss AI Center for SMEs (CSIA-PME)
texte:
Let us make safe and secure AI accessible to all Swiss SMEs.

Paula Reichenberg, CEO and founder of Neur.on, has recently been appointed to the Industrial Board of the Swiss AI Center for SMEs (CSIA-PME), led by HES-SO University of Applied Sciences and Arts Western Switzerland.

For a committed start-up founder and LegalTech CEO, taking on an extra responsibility is not an obvious choice.

However, the Swiss AI Center, co-founded by Professor Jean Hennebert to serve small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and ICT start-ups, takes such a pragmatic, entrepreneur-focused approach that Paula was convinced she could contribute simply by voicing the pressing needs of innovative companies in Switzerland. To name just a few: data sovereignty and the matching Swiss GPU infrastructure, transparency of data sources and data flows in generative AI, and clear, business-compatible guidelines and rules for AI certification.

We look forward to exchanges with entrepreneurs from every sector.

titre: Neur.on opens its doors for FribourgOpen, organised by the CCIF
texte:
Last Wednesday, Neur.on opened its doors for FribourgOpen, an event organised by the CCIF (Chamber of Commerce and Industry of the canton of Fribourg).

All available places were quickly booked: the room was full of AI enthusiasts who took part in hands-on learning and got a look behind the scenes of engineering. Throughout the event, participants immersed themselves in the fast-moving world of natural language processing. They rolled up their sleeves and worked through practical exercises, gaining a first-hand understanding of the details behind Neur.on’s AI capabilities. Events like this allow us to share our passion for innovation. They are also lively platforms for knowledge sharing and networking.

We warmly thank the CCIF for this opportunity, and everyone who joined us.

titre: e-forum 2023: the metaverse, AI, cybersecurity & co., opportunities and challenges for companies
texte:
In September 2023, the eForum in Zurich looked at the finer points of the metaverse, AI and cybersecurity.

Paula Reichenberg, CEO of Neur.on, moderated a discussion on the ‘Pains and Gains’ of digitalisation.

The panel featured Dr Luba Schönig, co-founder of UMushroom, and Marcel Gygli, a professor specialising in AI in the public sector at the University of Bern.

Participants gained useful insight into companies that have integrated AI smoothly into their operating model. They also gained a better understanding of the societal, ethical and data security issues that will be decisive in the future. The analyses of AI’s impact on the public sector and the business world sparked a lively dialogue with the audience. It highlighted the concerns shared by both employees and decision-makers in the sector.

titre: Neur.on joins Trust4SMEs, Trust Valley’s cybersecurity programme for SMEs
texte:
We are pleased to announce our admission to Trust Valley’s prestigious ten-month Trust4SMEs support programme, dedicated to cybersecurity and digital trust for SMEs.

Our LegalTech company serves law firms, the Big Four, banks, insurance companies and public authorities: data security is deeply rooted in our values.

From the outset, we made the deliberate choice to meet the most demanding standards in information and AI security (ISO 27001 and CertAI standards), an early commitment that may seem unusual for a start-up.

But we firmly believe that cybersecurity should not be an afterthought, postponed until revenue starts flowing in.

True to this commitment, we have decided to invest all the time and resources needed to walk the talk.

With this in mind, we warmly thank Trust Valley and the more than 40 partners of the Trust4SMEs programme for their support throughout our journey, including the Canton of Vaud, the Republic and Canton of Geneva and EPFL Innovation Park, as well as our coach Laura Tocmacov of the impactIA Foundation.

titre: Neur.on among Switzerland’s top AI start-ups, according to Startupticker

titre: Neur.on wins first prize in the elevator pitch competition at the Weblaw LegalTech forum
texte:
Thank you to the LegalTech champions.

We would like to thank Weblaw, Coop Rechtsschutz AG, YLEX and UBS for actively supporting Swiss LegalTech start-ups.

Delivering an elevator pitch is never a start-up founder’s favourite sport. But for LegalTech players, whose products are always seen as technical and, to be honest, a little boring, the exercise can be particularly thankless.

Being able to pitch to a savvy, tech-friendly audience of legal professionals and potential clients was therefore a much appreciated privilege.

And of course, winning first prize through the audience vote is particularly rewarding.

Long live the Weblaw LegalTech forum.

titre: Neur.on at the LegalTech Summer Eve in Geneva: will AI change NOTHING for lawyers?
texte:
Tonight, Geneva lawyers are discussing LegalTech with the makers of their favourite tools, EyeTeK and Neur.on.

Among the ‘disruptive theses’ presented tonight is one particularly risky and tempting claim:

AI will change NOTHING about the work of lawyers

Why? Because AI excels above all at tasks:

  • that lawyers DO NOT LIKE doing (checking the consistency of footnotes);
  • that lawyers DO NOT HAVE TIME to do (tagging and summarising the articles that interest them);
  • that some lawyers DO NOT KNOW how to do well (spelling, grammar, translation).

titre: Neur.on joins the debate at the Lawyers’ Congress 2023 (Anwaltskongress)
texte:
The Lawyers’ Congress 2023 marks the 125th anniversary of the Swiss Bar Association. A good reason to celebrate.

Yet Swiss lawyers have never felt so worried about the future of their profession.

The Neur.on team looks forward to contributing to the discussions and to showing that well-designed technology can be a force for good. It can increase not only efficiency (a prospect that may seem daunting) but also, and above all, profitability and quality of life.

titre: Neur.on joins the debate on data security at a CCIF conference
texte:
Data security is a major issue for lawyers and the cornerstone of the services Neur.on offers. The crucial role of using industrial data is under debate today at the conference “Industrial data: a resource to tap”, organised by the CCIF, Chamber of Commerce and Industry of the canton of Fribourg at HEIA-FR (School of Engineering and Architecture of Fribourg).

Our CTO, Yann-Ivain Beffa, is contributing to the debate with his presentation “AI applied to text: should we build a data refinery?”.

titre: Neur.on pitches at the first edition of the Fri Up Startup Lunches
texte:

It was a privilege to take part in the first Start-Up Lunch presented by Fri Up, the official business start-up support organisation of the canton of Fribourg, and to receive kind feedback from an audience of experts and potential clients.

titre: Neur.on discusses the future of the legal sector at the Zukunft Rechtsmarkt 2023 conference
texte:
The legal profession faces many paradigm shifts, driven by disruptive new technologies, a changing society and an ever more competitive job market.

Legal service providers must embrace this change to survive. Neur.on is ready to help them adapt with its AI-driven translation platform, built from the ground up to meet the exacting needs of legal and financial professionals.

Our founder, Paula Reichenberg, was invited to speak at the session “The future of the legal field” of the University of St.Gallen (HSG) on 4 May in Zurich. Paula joined experts from across Swiss law to share her view of the role of LegalTech in the law firm of the future.

titre: Neur.on CTO Yann-Ivain Beffa presents “AI for Legal document Analysis” at the AI Days
texte:
ChatGPT and Dall-e have captured the public imagination and opened the world’s eyes to the remarkable potential of artificial intelligence. Because these solutions are general-purpose and accessible, they have sparked interest in every sector, including those seen as more conservative, such as the legal profession. Lawyers are looking for secure solutions, custom-built by experienced specialists to fit their needs and processes.

This is where Neur.on comes in. In two Innosuisse projects, we combine proprietary algorithms and a carefully built data corpus within human-in-the-loop processes, to offer new specialised AI capabilities in LegalTech.

Yann-Ivain Beffa, CTO of Neur.on, gave a talk on “AI for Legal document Analysis” at the first edition of the AI Days, an event organised by the newly created Swiss AI Center for SMEs, an initiative supported by HES-SO University of Applied Sciences and Arts Western Switzerland, with iCoSys as a key partner.

Read the full article.

titre: Neur.on plays an active role at Words to Deeds 2023, a major European legal translation event
texte:
The rise of machine translation brings with it the risk of serious errors in legal translations.

More than ever, law firms need to make translation diligence part of their quality assurance cycle.

This weekend, lawyers and legal translators from across Europe will discuss and refine best practice in Cambridge, UK, at the Words to Deeds conference (W2D2023).

Neur.on CEO Paula Reichenberg will be a panellist in the session “Risks and Legal Tech”, sharing her view on the specific issues facing the LegalTech sector.

titre: Neur.on, first company in the ‘Linguistic Services’ category of the SLTA map
texte:
Neur.on has been added to the Swiss LegalTech Association (SLTA) map as the first company in the ‘Linguistic Services / Translation & Anonymization’ category.

Neur.on is delighted that the ‘Linguistic Services / Translation & Anonymization’ category has been newly created to put its AI-driven translation SaaS solution on the map of the Swiss LegalTech Association.

Neur.on uses specialised natural language processing models to offer Swiss legal professionals an end-to-end translation process, built from the ground up to meet their needs.

We look forward to being joined in this category by other promising start-ups: Andrea Schmidheiny Konic and Bojan Konic.

titre: Neur.on’s Christmas get-together for lawyers, LegalTech players and their families
texte:
AI is at the very core of Neur.on’s products and strategy. To create reliable and practical solutions, however, we must be fully aware of AI’s limits and accept them. We make up for them with ingenuity, inventiveness and the many other purely human skills that machines will NEVER be able to match: warmth, camaraderie, conviviality and empathy.

We warmly thank all the lawyers and professionals of the LegalTech community, and their families, who joined us last Saturday for hot drinks and good laughs.

Special thanks to the wonderful team at Schipfe 16, supported by the Social Services Department of the City of Zurich, who made this event even more special with their professionalism and kindness.

We wish you and your families happy holidays.

titre: Innosuisse funds research and development of Neur.on’s translation SaaS
texte:
SWISS FUNDING POWERING SWISS AI: Innosuisse, the Swiss Innovation Agency, has recently granted us new funding for the research and development of Neur.on’s legal and financial translation SaaS.

Neur.on’s research project supported by Innosuisse will be carried out with the iCoSys institute (Institute of Complex Systems) of the School of Engineering and Architecture of Fribourg (HEIA-FR). The aim is to bring secure, reliable and efficient AI translation to Switzerland and to the rest of the world.

We will apply innovative zero-shot and few-shot learning approaches to specialised legal and financial NLP models, efficiently integrating user feedback when machine translation output is reviewed.

With this funding, we can continue developing the technical tools needed to build complex AI translation tools that are simple and accessible for legal and financial professionals.

Thank you to Innosuisse for its support.

titre: What lawyers in asset management expect from LegalTech: Neur.on at the LAM conference
texte:
What do lawyers working in asset management expect from LegalTech? What are the most effective strategies for selecting and implementing useful AI solutions in a legal department?

Being a lawyer in asset management takes many talents and a good dose of resilience, especially when you are a legal department of one. Facing an ever-changing regulatory environment and blurred compliance definitions, and juggling contract work with internal legal issues, lawyers in asset management could use all the help technology can give them.

Which LegalTech tools can they put in place immediately to get better, faster and cheaper results?

At the invitation of Andreas Hinsen and Julien Cayet of Loyens & Loeff, our CEO, Paula Reichenberg, and Jordan Urstadt of PartnerVine presented practical solutions and use cases at the inaugural Lawyers in Asset Management (LAM) conference, co-organised with Aruna Arasu of Alpha Associates and Nicky Walsh of Astra Legal.

texte:
We are proud to be members of the LegalTech community in Switzerland and to help lawyers across the country work more efficiently.

Hosted entirely in Switzerland and meeting the strictest data security standards, LexMachina enables lawyers to comply with all applicable ‘Security by Design’ requirements.

titre: Did you miss our presentation at the 14th AMTA conference?
texte:
AMTA is one of the most important conferences in the machine translation industry. It brings together experts and practitioners from research, industry and academia.

The 14th biennial conference of the Association for Machine Translation in the Americas (AMTA), held virtually from 6 to 9 October 2020, had three main tracks (Research, Commercial and Government), dedicated respectively to machine translation research, its commercial applications and its use by government. Over three days, AMTA brought together experts and practitioners from research, industry and academia, who shared the latest advances in machine translation R&D and presented and discussed real-world use cases.

Hieronymus was delighted to speak at AMTA 2020 Virtual.

Together with Rubén Martinez and Mārcis Pinnis of Tilde, Paula Reichenberg shared lessons learned from developing the first neural machine translation engine for the Swiss legal and financial market.
